PullRequest.Title: agentHost: Exclude SDK-native skills from directory discovery
PullRequest.Body:
## Problem

In Agent Host discovery mode, VS Code combines two Copilot runtime APIs that intentionally return different sets of data:

- `skills.getDiscoveryPaths()` returns directories where users can create skills, such as project, personal, and configured custom directories.
- `skills.discover()` returns every skill available to the runtime, including skills supplied by installed plugins and the runtime itself.

VS Code previously assumed that every item from `skills.discover()` belonged under a directory from `skills.getDiscoveryPaths()`. Copilot runtime 1.0.84-2 exposed that latent mismatch by returning installed-plugin skills. Because plugin and built-in skills do not have user-creatable discovery directories, VS Code created synthetic writable fallback directories for them and emitted an invariant error on every customization refresh:

`[SessionCustomizationDiscovery] BUG: customization '.../installed-plugins/.../SKILL.md' of type 'skill' is outside discovered directories`

In one recent Insiders session this repeated tens of thousands of times. The resulting directory entries were also projected into VS Code's synthetic session plugin even though plugin and built-in skills are SDK-native sources.

## Fix

Exclude skills whose SDK `source` is `plugin` or `builtin` before converting discovered skills into directory customizations.

This keeps the two ownership paths separate:

- SDK-native plugin and built-in skills remain owned and loaded by the Copilot runtime.
- Project, inherited, personal, and custom-directory skills continue to be represented by VS Code directory customizations.

The existing fallback and invariant error remain unchanged for directory-backed customizations that unexpectedly cannot be attributed to a discovery path. Using `excludeHostSkills` on the RPC request would not be appropriate because it would also hide legitimate personal and configured custom-directory skills.

## Testing

Added a regression test that returns plugin, built-in, and project skills from the SDK and verifies that:

- plugin and built-in skills are excluded from directory customizations;
- the project skill remains under its reported discovery directory; and
- no fallback error is emitted for the SDK-native skills.

Validation:

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/sessionCustomizationDiscovery.test.ts` - 44 passing
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- pre-commit hygiene checks

(Written by Copilot)

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed loop, exact-file cardinality, sequential awaits, filesystem boundary, and startup await chain are explicit in code. Exact wall-clock impact varies with plugin count and filesystem cache, which is why severity is medium rather than high.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For N distinct SDK-reported plugin agent/rule/skill files, findPluginRoot performs a serial ancestor walk for each file; each ancestor incurs up to three sequential exists calls, so the new filesystem work grows as O(N × path depth) even when all N files belong to one plugin root.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased session-creation and customization-refresh latency from serialized filesystem I/O
Findings.PreviousBehavior: SDK-native plugin results were converted directly into directory children (with only the existing per-skill file read); discovery did not walk filesystem ancestors for every plugin agent, rule, and skill.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every plugin-sourced agent, rule, and skill URI is added to pluginFiles, then this loop awaits findPluginRoot separately for each exact file before deduplicating the resulting roots.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `for (const file of pluginFiles) { const root = await this.findPluginRoot(file, token); }` loop at lines 774-775 precedes root deduplication; the added findPluginRoot implementation checks three manifest locations at every ancestor.
Findings.Title: Coalesce plugin-root lookup before walking every child
Findings.Impact: Opening a chat/session with installed plugins, or refreshing customizations, waits for 4-7 serialized stats for each typical agent/rule/skill path; plugins with many contributions or users with several plugins add proportional I/O latency before customizations or the SDK session can be published.
Findings.Evidence: pluginFiles is an exact-URI ResourceSet populated by discoverAgents, discoverRules, and discoverSkills. At line 775 each URI is processed serially. findPluginRoot (lines 815-833) starts at that file's directory and issues up to three awaited IFileService.exists calls per ancestor. Only after all walks does pluginRoots deduplicate common roots. SessionDiscoveredEntry._refresh awaits discover, and both getCustomizationsSettled (used by getChatCustomizations) and getAppliedPlugins (used by session snapshots) await that refresh, placing these checks on chat/session startup. One plugin with multiple agents, rules, and nested skills therefore repeats the same root/ancestor probes.
Findings.Recommendation: Within one discovery pass, memoize/coalesce ancestor-to-root resolution (including in-flight and negative results) so sibling files reuse the first walk, then deduplicate roots before parsing. Preserve cancellation and avoid unbounded parallel stats.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Each SDK-native plugin child that was outside SDK discovery directories entered toDirectoryCustomizations and emitted an error-level invariant log on every discovery refresh, producing repeated log formatting and sink I/O proportional to plugin children and refreshes.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Large volumes of repeated SessionCustomizationDiscovery invariant errors and corresponding log I/O during customization refreshes.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Plugin-sourced agents, rules, and skills are now collected into plugin containers and filtered out before directory grouping, so they no longer hit the fallback/error path; the fallback diagnostic is also downgraded to trace for genuinely unexpected directory-backed entries.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The old base line 975 logged at error inside the per-customization fallback branch. The added filters at lines 601-603 remove plugin children from all three directory-grouping calls after source-tagged entries are collected, while line 982 changes any remaining invariant diagnostic to trace. SessionDiscoveredEntry reruns discovery on watched file and root-config changes, so the old per-child log repeated across refreshes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or open a Copilot chat/session when SDK-native plugins are installed
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SessionDiscoveredEntry starts discover on creation; getChatCustomizations waits in getCustomizationsSettled, and SDK session snapshots wait in getAppliedPlugins. The three SDK discovery calls must complete, followed by the newly added plugin-root resolution and plugin parsing, before customizations/plugins can be returned.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copilot runtime agents, instructions, and skills discovery RPCs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three RPCs per discovery pass, grouped concurrently and independent of N
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same three discovery RPCs already ran on this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All three must finish before plugin projection can begin

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Walk each plugin child URI upward and check up to three manifest locations per ancestor
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to roughly 3 × path-depth existence checks for each of N distinct plugin child files; common roots are deduplicated only afterward
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No ancestor manifest walk was performed for plugin-sourced agents or rules; plugin skills incurred their existing direct skill-file read only.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All checks are serially awaited before plugin parsing and session customization publication

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Detect format, read manifest, resolve component directories, and read plugin agents/skills/rules/hooks/MCP configuration
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full parse per D deduplicated plugin roots, with format and manifest redundantly read once before parsePlugin and again inside it
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: SDK-native plugin roots were not parsed by SessionCustomizationDiscovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Parsing is awaited before the plugin container is returned

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The effective input is the number N of distinct plugin-sourced agent, rule, and skill file URIs returned by the SDK, and D deduplicated plugin roots. N can substantially exceed D because each plugin contributes multiple files.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: agents.discover, instructions.discover, skills.discover, hook discovery, and watcher updates run concurrently. After they settle, plugin-root searches run serially across N files; each ancestor's manifest checks are also sequential. Plugin parsing then runs serially across D roots, although component reads within one parsePlugin call use Promise.all.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Discovery directories are cached per SessionCustomizationDiscovery instance, but plugin-file-to-root and parsed-plugin results are not. A fresh session is cold and repeats all root walks/parsing; OS or file-provider metadata caching may reduce individual stat cost but does not coalesce calls. No negative or in-flight root cache exists.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: exact-URI collection, post-walk root deduplication, sequential awaits, and the session startup await chain are all directly visible in code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Installed plugin counts, contributions per plugin, path depth, and filesystem cache warmth vary by user. The serialized N×depth boundary mechanism and critical-path placement are explicit; uncertainty affects severity, not causality.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium regression: root discovery repeats coalescible filesystem probes for every plugin child before deduplicating roots. The full per-root parse is required for the new projection behavior and was not separately reported.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh customizations after a watched file change or root configuration change
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A matching file event or root-config event schedules a debounced refresh. Discovery, plugin root resolution, and parsing complete before _onDidRefresh publishes SessionCustomizationsChanged; work is off the direct editor-input path but blocks the updated customization snapshot.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three concurrent RPCs per effective refresh
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These RPCs already ran on each discover refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Refresh cannot publish until they settle

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: O(N × path depth) serial existence checks per effective refresh
One parse per D root per effective refresh
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: SDK-native plugin directories were not parsed here.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fallback diagnostic logging for customizations outside discovered directories
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before this PR, one error-level log per unmatched plugin child per refresh; now plugin children bypass grouping and residual diagnostics are trace-level
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Plugin children could emit repeated error logs. This concrete regression fix was recorded with its introducing commit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The PR removes repeated high-level logging from this refresh path

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N distinct SDK-reported plugin files and D plugin roots on every effective debounced refresh; repeated events within 100 ms coalesce, events after settlement trigger another full pass.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The Delayer coalesces events within 100 ms and cancels an in-flight refresh when a newer one is queued. Within an effective pass, SDK discovery is concurrent but plugin-root walks and root parses are serial.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Only discovered directory paths are retained. Plugin-root resolutions and parsed plugin data are recomputed on each effective refresh; there is no warm application cache keyed by plugin root/content metadata.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: event sources, 100 ms coalescing, cancellation, refresh call path, and lack of plugin-root cache are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Refresh frequency depends on workspace activity and configuration changes. Debouncing bounds bursts, but each settled refresh still repeats the uncached N×depth work.
Scenarios.Verdict: The same reported boundary-fanout issue applies. Debouncing prevents per-event explosion but does not remove repeated work per effective refresh; the PR also fixes prior repeated error logging.

Scenarios.Scenario: Discover ordinary project/personal skills and ignore SDK built-in skills
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing concurrent SDK discovery completes; project/personal skills are parsed and grouped into discovered directories. Added source checks skip built-in skills and route only plugin skills to plugin projection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and parse non-plugin SKILL.md files
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per non-plugin skill; built-in and plugin entries now skip this direct read
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All skill sources with paths were read; the diff reduces work for built-in and plugin entries, with plugin contents later parsed once per root.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Reads must complete before directory customizations are returned

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of non-plugin skills and directory customizations; built-in skill count is filtered before file reads.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Skill parsing uses Promise.all across SDK skill results. Directory grouping is in-memory after discovery.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache is introduced. Existing skill files are reread per discovery pass; built-in entries now avoid that read.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The mix of built-in, plugin, and project skills varies, but source-based filtering behavior is explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional regression: built-in entries are cheaper, project/personal behavior is preserved, and plugin-specific new costs are covered by the submitted finding.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files and surrounding startup, refresh, parser, watcher, and session-snapshot paths. Submitted one medium boundary-fanout finding for serial per-child plugin-root filesystem walks and recorded the PR's concrete fix for repeated error-level discovery logging.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
